metadata.name: Claude Translate
metadata.author: kanaru313
metadata.description: Translates lyrics line by line with the Anthropic Claude API, keeping the singer’s voice and the lines in sync. Needs your own API key from console.anthropic.com; the lines, and the title, artist and lyrics when song context is on, are sent to Anthropic.

apiKeys.title: Anthropic API keys
apiKeys.subtitle: One or more keys; the next key is used when one is refused or out of quota

options.title: Natural
options.subtitle: How a native speaker would say it, keeping the feeling

options.title: Close to the original
options.subtitle: For learners, wording matches word by word

options.title: Poetic
options.subtitle: Rhyme and rhythm over strict wording, keep imagery

options.title: Singable
options.subtitle: Same syllables and rhythm, rhymes where the original rhymes

useSongContext.title: Send the song as context
useSongContext.subtitle: Sends the title, artist and lyrics when available, so pronouns and the story fit the song. Turn off for privacy or when the provider objects to explicit lyrics

retryUntranslated.title: Retry lines left in the source language
retryUntranslated.subtitle: When a line comes back unchanged and is not a name or sound, sends it again alone once to get it translated

temperature.title: Temperature
temperature.subtitle: 0 is deterministic, 1 more varied. Only applies to models that support Temperature

maxOutputTokens.title: Max output tokens
maxOutputTokens.subtitle: Ceiling on the answer length. 4096 fits a 60-line chunk well

customInstruction.title: Extra instruction for the model
customInstruction.subtitle: Appended to the prompt, e.g. "Prefer Southern Vietnamese pronouns"

systemPrompt.title: System prompt
systemPrompt.subtitle: Full prompt sent to Claude. Leave blank to use the default; place-holders {target_language}, {target_notes}, {style_prompt}, {song_prompt} and {custom_instruction} are filled in
systemPrompt.default:
You translate song lyrics into {target_language}. The source language is not given and may change from line to line: detect it for each line.

The user message is JSON. "lines" is a list of {"i": number, "t": text}: the lines to translate. "song", when present, describes the song and may hold its full lyrics: it is context only, never translate or return it.

Rules:
- Return a JSON object with a single key "lines": a list of {"i": number, "t": text, "l": detected_language}.
- Return exactly one item per input line, with the same "i". Never merge, split, drop, reorder or add lines, even when a sentence runs over several lines.
- "t" is the translation of that line alone; "l" is the language you detected for the original line, as a BCP 47 code ("ja", "en", "ko"; for Chinese always "zh-Hans" or "zh-Hant"). Give "l" for every line.
- A line already in {target_language}, or a line that is only a name, an ad-lib or a sound ("oh", "yeah", "la la la", "na na na"), comes back unchanged.
- The singer's voice stays the same over all lines: who "I" and "you" are, and the tone between them.
- Keep proper nouns and numbers. Add no notes, quotes, romanization or explanations.
- Output ONLY valid JSON, with no preamble or trailing text.

{target_notes}

{style_prompt}

{song_prompt}

{custom_instruction}
